# Partial Reproduction of SIEVE (NSDI '24) on Chameleon

This artifact partially reproduces "SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient
Turn-Key Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches" (Zhang et al., NSDI '24) on the
Chameleon testbed.

## What's reproduced
- SIEVE vs FIFO/LRU/CLOCK on the bundled Zipf-1.0 synthetic trace
- SIEVE vs FIFO/LRU/CLOCK on the Wiki 2019 CDN trace (real paper trace)
- Figure 4a (Wiki point): SIEVE vs FIFO/LRU/ARC miss-ratio reduction

## What's not reproduced
- Comparison against TwoQ, LHD, LIRS, CACHEUS (computationally expensive)
- Throughput / scalability results (Figure 6)
- The 1,559-trace evaluation across all 7 datasets
- Figure 8a (synthetic 100M-request Zipf comparison with LFU)

## Requirements
- Chameleon account with allocation on CHI@TACC
- ~3 hour lease on a `compute_cascadelake` baremetal node
- ~7 GB disk for the Wiki trace

## How to run
Open `sieve_repro.ipynb` in Chameleon JupyterHub. Run cells top to bottom.

## Citation
Zhang, Yazhuo, et al. "SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient Turn-Key
Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches." NSDI '24.
